articles.title: After coldest night, Indore sees hottest day of Sept in decade
articles.summary: Indore records decade-high September max of 35°C after coldest night; clear skies and no rain as monsoon withdrawal nears, with more heat expected.
articles.body: Indore: After recording its coldest Sept night in a decade, Indore on Wednesday registered its hottest Sept day in 10 years, as clear skies pushed the maximum temperature to 35 degrees Celsius, 2 degrees above normal. Tuesday’s maximum was 34.3 degrees Celsius, 1 degree above normal.The highest maximum temperature recorded in the city in the month was 37.4 degrees Celsius on Sept 27, 1987.On Tuesday, the city recorded its lowest night temperature for Sept in a decade after mercury dropped to 16.6 degrees Celsius.Despite rising daytime temperatures, the night remained relatively cool on Wednesday, with the minimum settling at 18.9 degrees Celsius, two degrees below normal. The city received no rain during the day. At 5.30 pm, the temperature was 30.8 degrees Celsius and relative humidity was 44%.Conditions are gradually becoming favourable for the southwest monsoon to withdraw from the remaining parts of Madhya Pradesh over the next two to three days, IMD Bhopal meteorologist Arun Sharma said.The withdrawal line currently passes through Gurdaspur, Chandigarh, Muzaffarnagar, Aligarh, Dholpur, Udaipur, Deesa and Naliya, among other locations. The monsoon is likely to withdraw from the remaining parts of Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh and most of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh in the next two to three days, the weather department said. Further withdrawal is expected from all of Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, and parts of Bihar, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra.The Met department has forecast a gradual two- to three-degree rise in maximum temperature over the next two days, followed by no significant change. With clear skies and the monsoon retreating, maximum temperatures in Indore may remain elevated in the coming days. articles.title: Saudi Arabia not to compromise on security as Houthis choose ‘chaos’: MBS
articles.summary: Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman says the kingdom ‘will not hesitate to respond firmly to any threat’.
articles.body:
Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) has promised not to compromise on the kingdom’s security in the face of attacks by the Houthi armed group, saying the Yemeni rebels chose “chaos and destruction, threatening the Yemeni people and the region”.

In a speech delivered Wednesday on behalf of King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud during the opening of the third year of the ninth session of Saudi Arabia’s Shura Council, Prince Mohammed said the country “will not hesitate to respond firmly to any threat or attack aimed at undermining” its security.

He pointed to the trilateral Mecca Joint Defence Agreement with Turkiye and Pakistan that was formalised in August , saying the alliance shows the Saudi leadership’s intent “to strengthen regional stability, shield it from the repercussions of tensions and conflicts and coordinate efforts”.

At the same time, the crown prince said, Saudi Arabia is making “every possible effort to de-escalate tensions and support diplomatic solutions without the slightest compromise on preserving our security”.

MBS also addressed the targeting of vessels by the Houthis in the Red Sea along the Bab al-Mandeb strait, rejecting the use of international waterways as a tool for political or economic pressure.

He said a “multinational defensive maritime coalition” was set up to ensure “common interests” are protected in international waterways.

In recent weeks, the Houthis have ramped up attacks on Saudi Arabia, as they fight Yemen’s internationally recognised, Saudi-backed government forces.

Last week, Riyadh said it intercepted six ballistic missiles aimed at Taif in western Saudi Arabia and the Yanbu port area on the Red Sea.

The Houthis also said they attacked “a sensitive target” in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, and Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu.

On Tuesday, Pakistan’s Defence Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif said Islamabad will make “whatever means” available to Saudi Arabia under the mutual defence pact if the Houthi attacks on the kingdom continue.

articles.title: Netanyahu praises stabbed Indian pilot for saving lives on Flydubai flight
articles.summary: The Israeli prime minister thanks ‘true hero’ Captain Smit Machchhar for ‘extraordinary bravery’.
articles.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has thanked an Indian pilot, who was stabbed by a co-pilot, for saving 174 people on board the Flydubai Dubai-Tel Aviv flight that made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.

“My salute to the Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for his extraordinary bravery,” Netanyahu wrote on his official X account on Wednesday evening.

He said that despite being stabbed and seriously injured, Machchhar “fought back, resisted, opened the cockpit door, and enabled passengers and crew to overpower the attacker – preventing a catastrophic mid-air disaster”.

“He saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals,” Netanyahu said, adding that he wished the pilot “a speedy and full recovery”.

The co-pilot of the flight, who is accused of stabbing Machchhar in an alleged attempt to take control of the aircraft, remains unidentified, but Netanyahu said he was arrested after the plane landed in Saudi Arabia.

India’s embassy in Riyadh said “the brave Indian pilot of Flydubai” Smit Machchhar was, “admitted in a hospital in Tabuk city in northwest Saudi Arabia and receiving necessary medical attention”, in a post on X.

The embassy said it was awaiting a full update on the pilot’s health but that “he is reported to be in stable condition”.

Flydubai flight FZ1073 transmitted an emergency alert shortly after takeoff from Dubai on Wednesday morning, making an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia’s Tabuk airport with all passengers safe and accounted for, according to the airline.

Flight-tracking data from the Flightradar24 website indicated the flight was a Boeing 737 Max 8 aircraft.

A rescue flight – operated by Flydubai – flew all passengers from Tabuk to their final destination, Tel Aviv’s Ben Gurion airport at 15:34 GMT.

They were received at the airport by Netanyahu, in a display the Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid called “cheap politics”, in the run-up to this month’s elections.

articles.summary: PM Narendra Modi held a phone call with US President Donald Trump Wednesday to review bilateral cooperation in trade, defence, critical technologies and
articles.body: PM Narendra Modi held a phone call with US President Donald Trump Wednesday to review bilateral cooperation in trade, defence, critical technologies and energy, amid increasing friction in the relationship driven primarily by India’s purchase of Russian oil.Modi is learnt to have touched upon India’s concerns related to the US’ latest Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 (SRIA) that allows the president to impose up to 100 percent tariffs on countries like India and China for their procurement of Russian oil.In the run up to the Modi-Trump conversation – their first since they met in France in June – both external affairs minister S Jaishankar and foreign secretary Vikram Misri had flagged the same concerns with American authorities, emphasising the recently enacted SRIA would have consequences for India-US ties. India continues to maintain that its energy sourcing is driven by national interests and the need to ensure reliable and affordable supplies for 1.4 billion people.Modi said in a post on X that he had productive conversation with Trump. “We reviewed our bilateral cooperation in trade, defence, energy, critical technologies and other areas. We agreed to maintain close engagement to take our Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership forward,” said the PM, adding that they also exchanged views on regional and international issues, including ongoing efforts to advance global peace and security.An Indian readout said they agreed to maintain close engagement to deepen cooperation for the benefit of the people of both countries, and also to remain in touch. There was no White House readout till late in the evening.According to diplomatic sources, the conversation helped reinforce the strategic partnership amid the friction over the US passage of the Russia-related legislation, and also differences over trade that have prevented the 2 countries from concluding a bilateral trade agreement. Modi will travel to the US in December for the G20 summit in Florida where he is likely to also have a bilateral meeting with Trump. However, potential US tariffs or penalties could disrupt the diplomatic buildup to the visit.Jaishankar had raised India’s concerns related to the SRIA with his counterpart Marco Rubio in a meeting on the margins of the UNGA last week. Earlier this week, foreign secretary Vikram Misri told a visiting Congressional delegation that the new law will have a negative impact on not just bilateral relations but also the energy situation in global markets.Trade and energy, however, are not the only issues that India and the US need to address to get the relationship back on track. articles.title: Rochdale Council wins 'Downton Shabby' High Court case
articles.summary: Hopwood DePree took the council to court in his bid to take over the Grade II-listed mansion for £1.
articles.body:
An American man has lost his legal bid to take ownership of a historic mansion for £1.

Hopwood DePree, who claims ancestral links to the Grade II-listed Hopwood Hall in Middleton, Rochdale, said he was "incredibly disappointed" after a judge at the High Court in Manchester ruled against him.

DePree, an actor and filmmaker, argued a 2017 agreement with Rochdale Council gave him the option to buy the manor house after securing planning permission to restore and redevelop it.

However, Judge David Hodge KC found the conditions required for ownership of the property to transfer had not been met.

Despite its current state, Hopwood Hall was described as being in the top 10% of most important listed buildings in England, the court heard.

DePree's plans included a wedding venue, hotel accommodation and visitor attractions aimed at bringing the hall back to life.

However, Rochdale Council decided in 2022 not to transfer ownership of the hall to DePree and later locked him and a group of volunteers out of the site.

The court heard the legal costs were about £150,000, with the council expected to seek an order requiring DePree to pay them.

A Rochdale Council spokesperson said the council was pleased with the judgment.

"It's a shame that we had to endure a costly court battle to get to this point, as the time and money invested in this process could have been better spent on the hall itself," they said.

The spokesperson said more than £1.6m had been spent on the hall by the council and Historic England since 2017, and that investment in vital repairs would continue while its long-term future was "considered in due course".

They added that, once restored and refurbished, the building would be "used for the benefit of the wider community of Middleton who rightly cherish it as an important part of Middleton's rich and varied heritage".

DePree published a book about his campaign to restore the hall in 2022, titled Downton Shabby.

Speaking after the ruling, he said he was "incredibly disappointed" and described it as "a sad day".

He said he was discussing next steps with his legal team, adding: "We are not giving up. Hopwood Hall must be saved."

"I am getting messages from around the world from people offering money and support," he added.

articles.title: Black Sabbath film difficult to watch, says Tony Iommi
articles.summary: The legendary band's Back To The Beginning concert at Villa Park will be released next month.
articles.body:
Black Sabbath guitarist Tony Iommi said a new film of the band's last ever performance was "emotional" and "difficult to watch".

The legendary heavy metal group's Back To The Beginning gig at Villa Park in Birmingham last year has been turned into a movie and will be released next month.

Iommi co-founded the band in the 60s alongside Ozzy Osbourne, who died two weeks after the concert, aged 76, Terence "Geezer" Butler and Bill Ward.

However, 78-year-old Iommi said he had seen the footage and was sure that fans would like it.

"I mean I've watched the footage and it's emotional. I've watched it only twice now," he said.

"I find it difficult to watch it, to be honest, because obviously [of] our relationship with each other. But I'm sure people will like it."

Iommi, nicknamed the Godfather Of Heavy Metal, received a "very special" honour on Wednesday for services to music and charity.

The musician was made a Member of the Order of the British Empire by the Princess Royal at Windsor Castle and said Ozzy "would have been pleased".

"I mean, I've got a lot of awards over the years... but this is very special to me, because [it is] from our own country, from England, so yeah really great," he said.

Ozzy died of a reported heart attack while suffering from several health conditions including Parkinson's disease.

Iommi said it had been "up and down" since his death, adding, "I've just kept busy, really".

Born in Birmingham in 1948, Iommi almost did not pursue a career in music after being told he might never play again when he lost the tips of two fingers on his right hand during an industrial accident.

But he later met drummer Ward and, in 1968, the pair formed a heavy blues rock band based in Birmingham - enlisting bassist Butler and frontman Osbourne to form what was then called Earth Blues Company.

The group later changed their name to Black Sabbath, and went on to sell millions of records over the next decade with tracks including Paranoid and War Pigs.

"We came up with something completely different in those days, which was really difficult to get through, but the whole thing is belief, believing in what you do, and we love what we've done," Iommi said.

articles.title: Country hitmaker reveals how faith carried him through son's murder — and toward compassion for his killer
articles.summary: Casey Beathard reveals how faith led him to reconcile with his son Clay's killer in the Fox Nation special, "Chords of Faith," narrated by Ainsley Earhardt.
articles.body: Legendary country music songwriter and former college football player Casey Beathard opened up about the tragic stabbing death of his son, Clay, revealing how his faith helped guide him through the unimaginable event. In the new Fox Nation special, "Chords of Faith," narrated by "Fox & Friends" co-host Ainsley Earhardt, Beathard explained how his trust in God allowed him to forgive the convicted killer Michael Mosley for his actions on that fateful December night in Nashville. "It was just going to kill me to carry all this weight, all this stuff," he said. "You know, I realized in the wake of this whole process that the more you dig into the Word of God, that he could be trusted with justice. And vengeance, you know, it's not mine, because that was just gonna weigh on me. Vengeance was God, it helped me [be] free and let me let it go." MICHAEL MONSOOR HAD AN ESCAPE ROUTE — THE MEDAL OF HONOR RECIPIENT CHOSE TO SAVE HIS TEAMMATES INSTEAD Beathard described the great pain he felt for Mosley, explaining that he "wasn't loved growing up" and expressed his sympathy for the Tennessee man convicted of killing his son. "Because this kid, honestly, when I looked across the room at this kid, it was so sad for a young kid to have to spend his whole entire life in prison," he said. "His parents weren't there, and I think he was looking for love and found love in the wrong, wrong, wrong places." Clay, a 22-year-old quarterback for the Long Island University Sharks football team, and his friend Paul Trapeni III, 21, were killed in December 2019 outside The Dogwood bar in Nashville. Attorneys said Mosley pulled a knife during a fistfight, resulting in the deaths. Mosley was charged and convicted of first-degree murder in March 2022 and sentenced to two consecutive life sentences plus 40 years. RILEY GREEN THOUGHT HE'D 'FRAME HOUSES FOR THE REST OF MY LIFE' BEFORE BECOMING A COUNTRY MUSIC STAR "Chords of Faith" goes beyond Beathard's family tragedy and into his storied music career. After playing college football at Elon University, in 1991, he moved to the Music City and never looked back, working at the Country Music Hall of Fame and the Bluebird Café before signing a songwriting contract that launched his success. Beathard wrote songs for some of the most prolific country music artists, including Kenny Chesney, Eric Church and George Strait. Many of his hit songs topped the Billboard Hot Country and Country Airplay charts, including Tracy Byrd's "Ten Rounds with Jose Cuervo," Chesney's "Don't Blink" and Church's "Hell of a View." "Casey's one of the best songwriters this town's ever known," Chesney said on the show. "[He] changed my life." ELLA LANGLEY SAYS 'CHOOSIN' TEXAS' SUCCESS IS 'CHANGING MY LIFE' AFTER HER SONG BREAKS MARIAH CAREY'S RECORD Church credited Beathard for writing relatable music, boasting that he does it "probably better than anyone at incorporating what we all experience in everyday life." Beathard remains an inspiration to his children, not only for his chart-topping hits but also for his unwavering dedication to fatherhood, especially in the wake of Clay's death. His eldest son, C.J., an NFL quarterback, praised both his father and mother, Susan, for their strength and resilience through the tragedy — maintaining they set a lasting example for their children. "It was hard on us, but for the parents, it's tough," C.J. said. "And to see the way my mom and dad handled that was very inspiring for us all as siblings." articles.title: 2 killed, 1 hurt in Virginia workplace shooting; suspect also dead, police say
articles.summary: Two men are dead and another is in critical condition after their coworker opened fire on them at a business in Manassas, Virginia, police say.
articles.body: Two men are dead and another is in critical condition after their coworker opened fire on them at a business in Manassas, Virginia, police say. The suspect, 37-year-old Marvin Grant, went to work Wednesday morning at United Rentals at 9415 Wellington Road and told a coworker that three people were going to die, Manassas City Police Chief Douglas Keen said. “There was some kind of altercation this morning,” Keen said. “He then pulled a pistol from his waistband and shot the three victims.” The victims were rushed in critical condition to a hospital, where two of them died of their injuries later in the morning. Police identified the victims who died as Richard Lamont, 48, and Christopher Serrano, 33. An online fundraiser for Serrano’s family says he was a devoted partner and father to a 10-year-old boy and 3-year-old girl. Keen said he personally knew Lamont, a father who coached youth football in Fauquier County for years. “September’s been a rough month. We lost a 16-year-old. Now I lost somebody I actually coached youth football with. And knowing what his commitment was and knowing his children and now fatherless, it hits home. It hits home for our community,” Keen said, referring to a shooting earlier this month that killed a 16-year-old girl in Manassas. The third person who was shot is stable but will need to undergo surgery, Keen said. A statewide manhunt for Grant came to end hours later on Interstate 81 in Augusta County, police said. Police had tracked the suspect using technology, and a Virginia state trooper spotted Grant’s car on southbound I-81, police said. Troopers tried to stop Grant after his car pulled into the rest area at the 232-mile marker, police said. Grant got out of the car, but then got back in and kept driving southbound on I-81, according to state police. Then troopers initiated a chase before Grant pulled over on the side of the road at the 227-mile marker. State police said they brought in a negotiator after seeing Grant had a gun. The standoff lasted for about an hour before the suspect shot himself, state police said. Grant was pronounced dead at a nearby hospital. Virginia State Police said no troopers fired their weapons. The shooting at United Rentals happened in a garage area of the business. Keen said at least eight employees were there at the time. He said there was no clear motive yet. “That brings no relief to our victims’ families. We’ve got to figure out what happened here, what caused this,” Keen said. During the response and subsequent manhunt, police told people to avoid the area and stay indoors as officers investigated. Officers blocked off access to Wellington Road and the Route 28 Bypass as they searched the area. Nearby schools were placed on lockdowns early Wednesday morning. Those lockdowns have since been lifted. Students at nearby Jennie Dead Elementary School were redirected to Metz Middle School.

articles.title: Cornell agrees to outside review into university's handling of gang rape allegation, Hochul says
articles.summary: Hochul discussed the case during an exclusive interview Wednesday afternoon at her Midtown offices and said "people need to know the truth."
articles.body:
Cornell University agreed Wednesday to initiate an independent investigation into how the Ivy League school handled what a former student now alleges was fraternity house gang rape, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul said on Wednesday.

Hochul discussed the case during an exclusive interview Wednesday afternoon at her Midtown offices. The governor sits on the Cornell University board.

The governor called for the outside review , saying what happened raised "serious questions about Cornell campus culture" and whether the university is doing all it can to protect students.

"I wanted to make sure they knew how important this was, and they absolutely agreed. And they're acting on this this afternoon. So, they'll be reporting on what the details are, but they will be conducting what I asked for, which is an independent outside investigation of what happened," Hochul said.

"People need to know the truth and I think it's important for the public, for the victim, her family and the university community to know that their university did everything that they're supposed to do."

Cornell's internal data show 35% of undergraduate women reported experiencing sexual assault during their time on campus but Hochul said the problem acute on every campus.

"There's been a culture of this kind of treatment of young women on campuses for as long as I've been in college, and it has to change. There has to be an awakening and an awareness that says enough is enough," Hochul said.

Earlier this week, as outrage over the allegations grew, the Tompkins County district attorney decided to reopen a criminal investigation into what happened . The move followed an earlier decision not to pursue a prosecution.

District Attorney Matthew Van Houten previously explained the legal reasoning behind that decision.

"If you are voluntarily intoxicated or under the influence of drugs, such that your judgement is impaired, that does not legally, under the penal law, constitute your inability to consent," Van Houten said.

An attorney for the woman who made the allegation welcomed the decision to reopen the case.

"I think the D.A. reopening this case is long overdue. Part of this issue I had with this case all along from a criminal standpoint is my client was traumatized," attorney Thomas P. Giuffra said.

The accuser, who was a 20-year-old Cornell student at the time, described some of that trauma in a text message exchange with a Chi Phi fraternity brother who she said invited her to the house in October 2024.

In messages obtained by ABC News, the woman, identified as "Jane Doe," wrote: "I will also say this is f-king RUINING my life temporarily. My reputation is destroyed and I'm utterly ashamed."

articles.title: Hong Kong journalist arrested on sedition charge
articles.summary: Authorities detain media founder over Prince Edward station clash video, as press freedom groups voice concern.
articles.body:
Hong Kong police have arrested an independent journalist on suspicion of incitement by spreading disinformation, local media report.

Tang Ho-wing, founder of the online Boom News, was arrested on Wednesday morning, according to Hong Kong news outlet Sing Tao. The publication displayed a photo of the alleged moment of arrest.

Boom News covered an incident on August 31 commemorating the seventh anniversary of the Prince Edward station clash between antigovernment protesters and police, where protesters claimed some were killed.

The outlet, which has more than 66,000 followers on Instagram, posted a video featuring a woman’s account of the 2019 events.

Authorities denied the allegations, and police said on Wednesday that rumours of deaths during the clash were baseless.

Hong Kong journalists face mounting restrictions under sweeping political changes triggered by Beijing’s 2020 national security law and reinforced by a local 2024 statute.

The chilling effect on the press became starkly visible in February, when Apple Daily founder Jimmy Lai was sentenced to 20 years in prison. Several of Lai’s former staff members received sentences ranging from nearly seven to 10 years.

Police said on Wednesday they arrested two people on suspicion of committing seditious acts under the 2024 national security law. Authorities did not name the suspects, but the South China Morning Post identified the second arrested as activist Lee Ying-chi.

According to authorities, the arrests stemmed from an August 31 gathering outside a subway station, where people carried flowers, chanted banned slogans, and allegedly spread disinformation intended to incite hatred against the government and police.

Six others previously arrested in connection with the same offence were later released on bail.

articles.title: Panel eyes 'debundling' of exam responsibilities
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Question-paper setting, exam conduct, test centres and security will be handled by separate agencies under a restructuring being prioritised by
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Question-paper setting, exam conduct, test centres and security will be handled by separate agencies under a restructuring being prioritised by the Nandan Nilekani-led task force on exam reforms. This "debundling" of responsibilities is central to a plan that also envisages exam centres in every district and a common calendar for major testing bodies.Separating the functions could limit concentration of control over the process. The panel is also planning a common calendar involving NTA, SSC, IBPS and RRBs.Test facilities to move closer to candidatesA common calendar for major testing bodies — NTA, SSC, Institute of Banking Personnel Selection and Railway Recruitment Boards — could help bring in coordinated scheduling to reduce clashes. It could further allow better use of exam infrastructure throughout the year.Centres in every district would bring testing facilities closer to candidates, particularly those in rural areas. The plan comes as the education ministry develops a national computer-based testing infrastructure strategy to support the migration of pen-and-paper entrance examinations, including NEET-UG.According to a govt official, the strategy aims to close geographic gaps in test-centre availability and establish uniform standards for examination facilities.Ashish Mittal, managing director of examination security provider Innovatiview, said: “The focus must be on ensuring that technology, physical infrastructure, security and operations integrate into one auditable examination system with candidate experience at the epicentre.”Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Supreme Court allows sale, manufacture of next-generation green firecrackers
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Ahead of the festive season, Supreme Court on Wednesday paved the way for the manufacture and sale of next-generation joined green firecrackers
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Ahead of the festive season, Supreme Court on Wednesday paved the way for the manufacture and sale of next-generation joined green firecrackers after Centre's recommendation. Commonly known as 'ladi', these were earlier banned by the court.SC also said a separate order would be passed for Delhi and indicated that while the bursting of firecrackers would not be banned, the activity would not be allowed at all hours.Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told a bench of justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale that government had recommended that joined firecrackers, which complied with norms fixed by Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI), be allowed. The issue of using barium chemical remains undecided as the ASG told the bench that field trials were on, and sought time till Oct 15.Submitting the findings of CSIR-NEERI, Bhati said the report said 25 braids were burst in one second in conventional joined firecrackers whereas in next-generation joined firecrackers, only five braids were burst in a second.Government said manufacturers must comply with specifications/formulations tested and approved by the competent authority as well as with the prescribed noise limit and emission and safety requirements fixed under the law.Advocate Pranav Sachdeva, appearing for some manufacturers, assured the bench they would do so.As the pollution crisis in winter has become an annual affair in Delhi, the bench said it would pass a separate order for the national capital. "We're making this very clear. Neither are we going to agree with you for a total ban nor are we going to allow it 24 hours," the court said.A total ban would have a "sentimental effect", SC said, but allowing bursting of crackers throughout the day would have a "huge impact on every other living being, including old people, sick people and children"."We need to find a solution whereby we can give specified time and we can specify what crackers are to be used," the bench told the petitioner seeking curbs on the sale of firecrackers in NCR.Earlier, two government organisations had taken contradictory stands in SC on allowing next-generation green firecrackers. While CSIR-NEERI approved them saying their pollution levels had decreased by 40-60% and recommended commercial production of flowerpots, sparklers, 'chakkars', pencils, 'ladis' and twinkling stars, Central Pollution Control Board said they contained barium nitrate, which was banned by SC.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Putin shows no sign of stopping the war as Russia doubles down on Ukraine
articles.summary: A foreign policy speech by the Russian president will be keenly watched, but all signs point to the full-scale invasion continuing.
articles.body:
When Vladimir Putin arrived to address Russia's parliament on Wednesday, a warm welcome was guaranteed.

"The Special Election Operation", as one Russian newspaper dubbed last month's legislative vote , has produced a State Duma even more pro-Putin than anything before it.

The ruling party, United Russia, now has more MPs than ever.

It allows the Kremlin to claim it has been handed a huge mandate from the Russian people.

Are there any signs he is prepared to halt what he calls the special military operation? Or should we brace for further escalation in Ukraine and in tensions with Europe?

On Thursday I'll be watching to see whether Russia's leader sheds light on his plans during an appearance at the Valdai Discussion Club in Moscow. Traditionally the president's speech at this annual foreign policy forum provides insight into Putin's world view.

Right now, everything points to Putin continuing Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine: despite his country's huge battlefield losses to date and the damage being done to Russia's economy.

Putin's speeches and statements suggest he remains confident that Russia can secure a military victory.

Judging by what is being reported in Russian media, Moscow is encouraged by the shortage of air defence missiles in Ukraine, as well as the expectation that Russian strikes this winter will increase pressure on Ukrainians. Kyiv has spoken of its difficulty in shooting down Russia's ballistic missiles and new jet-powered drones, which have been targeting Ukraine every day.

The Kremlin has made no secret of the fact it wants European states to slash their military and financial backing for Ukraine: the kind of support Moscow says is prolonging the war - or, rather, getting in the way of a Russian victory.

To achieve this, Western officials believe Russia has been sending not so subtle signals.

They accuse Moscow of waging an escalating hybrid war on European countries through cyber-attacks, acts of sabotage, and Russian drones violating European airspace. In Germany, a drone carrying an explosive device was found close to Ukrainian cargo planes at Leipzig airport.

A covert campaign in the "grey zone", that space between peace and war.

This week I asked Russia's foreign minister, Sergei Lavrov, does he admit that his country is waging a hybrid war against European countries?

"Do you mean when we destroy drones and missiles that Britain and continental Europe are supplying Ukraine with, and which are used to attack us?" Lavrov replied.

"If you admit your weapons are being used to strike us and we destroy them, call it whatever you want. But I have no doubt this is a war Europe is waging against us. We've been saying so for a long time."

That, indeed, has been the official Russian stance for some time: that what is happening in Ukraine amounts to a European war on Russia. It is a narrative that skips over the fact that in 2022 it was the Kremlin that launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and that Russia continues to wage war there.

How far would Russia go to sever European support for Kyiv?

Is Moscow, for example, actively preparing to initiate military conflict in Europe with a Nato member state? That seems unlikely. After more than four-and-a-half years of war Russia's army has not yet managed to occupy the whole of Ukraine's eastern Donbas region, right next door to Russia.

Fighting Europe may not be the plan, but freaking it out, to reduce support for Kyiv, could well be the intention.

"If they continue this war, a European war with American help, against Russia, on Ukrainian territory, sooner or later we'll feel the need to escalate," warns prominent foreign policy strategist Sergei Karaganov, honorary chairman of Russia's Council for Foreign and Defence Policy.

"According to my scenarios, the first series of blows will be conventional," he told me. "But if Europe does not surrender, unfortunately, we will have to go nuclear. There will be little left of some European countries."

But if Russia went nuclear there would be a response from Europe, and nothing would be left of Russia, I suggest.

"No, there will be no response from Europe," said Karaganov. "What, Britain will attack Russia with nuclear weapons? I hope you're not that crazy. I'm sure the Americans are not that crazy."

I asked him if he agreed the last four-and-a-half years had been disastrous for Russia, in terms of casualties and the worsening security and economic situation.

"We've lost a lot of people, yes," he admitted, "and I criticise my government for not being rough enough. But now we are getting rough enough in Ukraine. We're doing away with Ukraine as a viable state."

If "doing away with Ukraine as a viable state" is Moscow's goal, it is hard to imagine the war ending soon.

Meanwhile, Russia continues to rail against what it sees as the double standards of the West. In his recent address at the UN General Assembly, Sergei Lavrov accused the West of resorting to "brute force" around the world.

"What they did in Venezuela, was that soft power or brute force?" Russia's foreign minister asked me this week. He was referring to America's military operation in Caracas to capture Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro back in January.

"The fact that [the US] bombed and destroyed Iran's leadership, along with their families, including children, is that not brute force?"

But was Russia not resorting to brute force every day in Ukraine, I replied.

"If you mean the destruction of infrastructure used by a Nazi regime backed by the West to wage war on the Russian Federation, then we are resorting to brute force to eliminate this direct threat to us."

Not only is this another element of Russia' official narrative: painting Ukraine as a neo-Nazi state, creating a false pretext to justify Russia's actions.

With the admission of Russia's use of "brute force" in Ukraine, it is also further evidence that Moscow is in no mood to stop fighting.

articles.title: Trump announces $200bn South Korean investment in US, $54bn for Alaska LNG
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Wednesday announced about $200 billion in investments by South Korea in the United States, including $54 billion for a major
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Wednesday announced about $200 billion in investments by South Korea in the United States, including $54 billion for a major liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Alaska, as Washington and Seoul advance a broader $350 billion trade and investment agreement. The announcement was made at the White House alongside Alaska Senator Dan Sullivan, a key supporter of the project.South Korea on Thursday unveiled implementation plans for three major US energy projects under the investment package. They include the Alaska LNG project, a $22.3 billion gas-fired power plant in Texas and plans to invest $120 billion in eight nuclear reactors in the US.Trump described the Alaska project as one of the largest energy infrastructure investments in American history.“We’re thrilled to announce one of the largest energy infrastructure investments in American history,” Trump said.Alaska LNG projectThe Alaska project involves an 807-mile (1,300-kilometre) natural gas pipeline connecting the North Slope to an LNG export terminal in southern Alaska. The White House said the project would eventually help reduce energy costs for residents in the state.South Korea and the US will review the pipeline and terminal project, but it will proceed only if commercial and legal conditions are met.South Korea's investment in the wider package will be capped at $20 billion annually under a legally binding agreement. Profits will be split equally between South Korea and the US until Seoul recovers its principal investment across the projects.Trump repeatedly praised Sullivan, who has supported the Alaska gas project for years and is facing Democrat Mary Peltola in a competitive Senate race.“He’s got my ear, and he’s had my ear for a long time on Alaska," Trump said, adding that "all these energy projects are all mine, and I got ’em done working with Dan Sullivan.”Sullivan said the project would provide low-cost energy “for 50 to a hundred years” and estimated that it would create 12,000 construction jobs.“This is going to be the biggest LNG project in our country. We will be able to get gas, of course, to Alaskans first and to our military — and we need it — but to our Asian allies,” Sullivan said.Wider South Korean investmentThe investments stem from a $350 billion trade and investment agreement reached between Washington and Seoul in November 2025.Under the agreement, the US agreed to lower tariffs on South Korean cars, auto parts and other products from 25% to 15%. South Korea committed to invest $150 billion in US shipbuilding and another $200 billion in other strategic sectors.The Korean government said its planned energy investments include $120 billion for eight US nuclear reactors, including two based on South Korea's APR-1400 design. Specific details of the nuclear projects have not yet been decided.South Korea and the US will also launch a 6.47-gigawatt gas-fired power project in Encinal, Texas, to supply electricity directly to artificial intelligence data centres. Commercial operations are scheduled to begin in 2029.The Texas project is the first initiative selected by South Korea under its $200 billion strategic investment programme.Trump promotes economic recordThe announcements come as Trump prepares for a month-long campaign to promote his administration's economic and other policies ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.Republicans are seeking to retain control of both chambers of Congress, while Democrats are targeting seats including those in Alaska and Iowa.Trump has acknowledged that his administration needs to do more to highlight its achievements.“We have to turn this around,” he said on Wednesday.“I’ve done a very bad job of explaining," the president said at an earlier White House event.Trump is scheduled to travel to Texas and Alabama on Thursday, followed by Ohio on Saturday and Nebraska on Monday.You use AI every day.
